papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Safer Extensible Kernels
papers.takeaway: A synthetic kernel extension mechanism isolates untrusted modules while preserving a narrow, inspectable interface.

story.background: Operating-system kernels often extend privileged behavior through modules that share a large trusted computing base.
story.villain: One faulty extension can corrupt kernel memory, and coarse isolation makes frequent extension calls expensive.
story.approach: The fictional design combines capability-scoped memory access with a checked eBPF-style call boundary.
story.impact: The fixture demonstrates how a systems mechanism, its assumptions, and its group signal appear in the interface.
story.evaluation: A synthetic prototype comparison uses microbenchmarks and a toy storage service; no reported number is real.
story.limitations: The imaginary design assumes special compiler instrumentation and does not cover device firmware.
story.phd_group_signal: This fictional group favors implementation-heavy operating-systems work with explicit security boundaries.

papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Debugging Geo-Distributed Services
papers.takeaway: A fictional tracing system connects symptoms across regions without collecting every event from every service.

story.background: Distributed services scatter requests across machines and regions, so a single failure can leave evidence in many logs.
story.villain: Centralizing every trace is expensive, while sampling can discard the rare causal chain an operator needs.
story.approach: The made-up system builds compact causal sketches near each service and requests detailed traces only after an anomaly.
story.impact: The synthetic example supports phrase search across observability, geo-distribution, and trace analysis.
story.evaluation: A fictional trace replay compares storage overhead and diagnosis coverage on generated incidents.
story.limitations: The example assumes clocks have bounded drift and does not model malicious services.
story.phd_group_signal: This invented group combines distributed-systems prototypes with production-style trace analysis.

papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Finding Isolation Failures
papers.takeaway: A fabricated state-aware fuzzer explores container boundary failures while recording which runtime transitions exposed them.

story.background: Container runtimes combine kernel isolation primitives with privileged setup code and complex lifecycle transitions.
story.villain: Ordinary fuzzers mutate isolated calls but miss failures that require a precise sequence of namespace and privilege changes.
story.approach: The fictional tool learns a small transition model and directs mutations toward unexplored security states.
story.impact: This adjacent-systems fixture illustrates security-venue screening without implying that every security paper belongs in the corpus.
story.evaluation: A synthetic dynamic-analysis study exercises invented runtime implementations and seeded bugs.
story.limitations: The example considers one operating-system family and cannot establish exploitability.
story.phd_group_signal: The imaginary lab works at the boundary of systems security, testing, and runtime internals.

papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Recovering Shared Flash Without a Global Pause
papers.takeaway: A made-up recovery protocol rebuilds flash metadata incrementally so unaffected tenants continue issuing requests.

story.background: Shared flash services maintain metadata that maps many tenants' logical data to physical devices.
story.villain: A metadata failure can force a full scan and pause unrelated tenants during recovery.
story.approach: The fictional protocol isolates recovery epochs and reconstructs only metadata reachable by active requests.
story.impact: This fixture exercises storage, reliability, European geography, award, and code filters.
story.evaluation: A synthetic prototype replays generated storage traces against imaginary recovery baselines.
story.limitations: The example assumes replicated allocation logs and does not address simultaneous device loss.
story.phd_group_signal: The fictional group studies storage internals through prototypes, fault injection, and trace replay.

papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Congestion Control With Explicit Uncertainty
papers.takeaway: A synthetic transport protocol exposes uncertainty in path estimates before it changes its sending rate.

story.background: Congestion controllers infer network capacity from delayed and noisy acknowledgements.
story.villain: A controller that treats an uncertain estimate as fact can oscillate or overfill queues.
story.approach: The fictional design tracks a confidence interval and switches between probing and conservative modes.
story.impact: The record demonstrates networking, formal-model, simulation, and United Kingdom filters.
story.evaluation: An imaginary simulator and small emulation testbed compare queue delay across generated paths.
story.limitations: The fixture does not model adversarial receivers or wireless mobility.
story.phd_group_signal: The invented group pairs transport modeling with implementation and controlled experiments.

papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Carbon-Aware Serverless Placement
papers.takeaway: A fictional serverless scheduler shifts flexible work across regions while keeping latency constraints visible.

story.background: Serverless platforms place short functions across regions with different capacity, delay, and energy conditions.
story.villain: Optimizing only immediate latency can concentrate flexible work where the synthetic carbon signal is highest.
story.approach: The made-up scheduler separates hard latency budgets from a configurable carbon-aware placement objective.
story.impact: The fixture exercises incomplete-2026, cloud, energy, production-deployment, and Europe filters.
story.evaluation: A fabricated deployment replay uses generated demand and carbon traces; it makes no real environmental claim.
story.limitations: The imaginary approach assumes regional signals are timely and functions can move without data-residency constraints.
story.phd_group_signal: The fictional collaboration studies datacenter scheduling with operational constraints and trace-driven evaluation.

papers.title: [Synthetic fixture] Compositional Proofs for Shared Memory
papers.takeaway: A fabricated proof framework composes small memory-safety arguments into a model of a concurrent runtime.

story.background: Concurrent runtimes combine allocators, synchronization, and unsafe low-level code whose invariants interact.
story.villain: Verifying each component alone does not show that their assumptions remain true when the components share memory.
story.approach: The fictional framework expresses rely-guarantee contracts and checks their composition in a theorem prover.
story.impact: This adjacent-systems fixture exposes formal verification, runtime, proof, and artifact filtering.
story.evaluation: A synthetic proof case study covers invented allocator and scheduler models; no real theorem or artifact is claimed.
story.limitations: The imaginary proof assumes sequential consistency and omits device interaction.
story.phd_group_signal: The fictional group emphasizes formal models connected to low-level runtime mechanisms.
